Added eight portable cases in [tests.yaml](tests.yaml), preserving its invariant format. Coverage includes boundaries, duplicates, Unicode values, non-mutation, fresh results, and seeded stream replay.

Documented assertion and replay semantics in [FIXTURES.md](FIXTURES.md), with derivations and rule mapping in [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md).

Validated YAML, nine unique case IDs, and all documented fields. Implementation conformance remains untested. Uniformity remains unspecified by the contract.

Full conformance requires a nonempty requested suite, complete accounting, all required assertions executed and passed, and trustworthy harness evidence. A requested subset can conform within that scope; it does not establish whole-library conformance. No fixture suite proves correctness on every possible input.

## Negative controls

For a newly created or changed harness, prove relevant paths detect failure in disposable copies:

- Change one expected value and require a failure naming that case.
- Inject a wrong implementation return to exercise its API mapping/comparator.
- Make an operation required to error return normally and require an error-case failure.
- When relevant, inject an unknown scenario/assertion and confirm it prevents full conformance; inject absent environment values to check isolation.

Do not modify original fixtures or leave injected faults in the final implementation. Record the injected change, command, case result, and nonzero exit. The controls should fail for the intended reason, not merely fail to import or compile. Reuse prior negative-control evidence only when the harness and relevant profile behavior are unchanged and identifiable.

## Diagnosis

Separate implementation failures, harness defects, conflicting contract artifacts, and environment/setup failures. Report unsupported behavior explicitly. Error assertions are part of the suite; replacing them with skips or weakening matching without a contract decision changes the verification claim.

Use [the conformance report](../templates/reports/conformance.md) for saved evidence.
# Rule-to-case coverage

Record source identity, selected domain, and fixture profile before mapping coverage.

| Rule location/ID | Required behavior | Case IDs or proposed cases | Status/gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Expected-value derivation

For computed or disputed fixtures: source rule, independent derivation/tool, inputs, result, and comparison policy.

## Runner requirements and checks

Record argument/error mapping, named helpers/scenarios, new assertion semantics, fixture parsing checks, unique-ID checks, and execution evidence if available. List uncovered rules and explain which are deliberately deferred.

# shuffle(seq, rng)
Return a new sequence with the same multiset and length. Do not mutate seq.
A fixed seed reproduces a stream within one implementation.
Different languages may use different PRNG algorithms and streams.

  - name: length
    seed: 1
    seq: [a, b, c]

# Rule-to-case coverage

Source: local `SPEC.md`, API `shuffle(seq, rng)`. Fixture profile: invariant
records in `tests.yaml:shuffle_invariants`; stable identities are record names.
There is no Git metadata, implementation, or conformance runner in this workspace.
Source content hashes and fixture validation evidence are recorded below.

| Rule location | Required behavior | Case IDs | Coverage and distinguishing failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SPEC.md`, line 2: same length | Preserve sequence length | Existing `length`; all eight added cases | Detect dropping or adding elements, including empty/singleton boundary failures. |
| `SPEC.md`, line 2: same multiset | Preserve exact values and multiplicities | `empty`, `singleton`, `all_equal`, `unequal_duplicate_counts`, `distinct_values`, `exact_unicode_values`, `seeded_stream_distinct`, `seeded_stream_duplicates` | Detect deduplication, replacement with a repeated element, or count changes that preserve length. Unicode case detects normalization or case folding. |
| `SPEC.md`, line 2: new sequence | Allocate a fresh result container | All eight added cases | Detect returning the input, special-casing short inputs by aliasing, or recycling one output buffer across stream calls. |
| `SPEC.md`, line 2: do not mutate | Preserve original input order and contents | All eight added cases | Detect in-place shuffling, clearing, sorting, or other visible input mutation; checks repeat on both replay streams. |
| `SPEC.md`, line 3 | Reproduce a seeded stream within one implementation | `seeded_stream_distinct`, `seeded_stream_duplicates` | Compare two independently initialized streams through 16 sequential calls, detecting replay divergence after the first result as well as at initialization. |
| `SPEC.md`, line 4 | Permit different PRNGs and streams across languages | Every case; replay semantics in `FIXTURES.md` | No exact shuffled outputs, cross-language comparisons, forced order changes, or statistical distribution checks. |

## Expected-value derivation

No byte hashes or exact PRNG outputs serve as behavioral expectations. Length,
multiset, and non-mutation oracles come directly from an independent snapshot of
the fixture input. For `unequal_duplicate_counts` and `seeded_stream_duplicates`,
the multiset is `{a: 3, b: 2, c: 1}` with length 6. `all_equal` has four occurrences
of `a`. `distinct_values` and `seeded_stream_distinct` have eight unique values.
The Unicode case has length 6 and five distinct exact strings: precomposed
U+00E9 occurs twice, while U+0065 U+0301, `A`, `a`, and the empty string each occur
once. Empty length is 0; singleton length is 1. Replay uses relational equality
between streams from the same implementation, never candidate-generated golden
outputs. Freshness uses container identity, not value expectations.

## Runner requirements and checks

`FIXTURES.md` defines argument mapping, exact comparisons, all new assertion
fields, the `draws` option, replay setup/actions/observations/cleanup, unsupported
requirements, and complete case accounting. The existing invariant container and
the original `length` record are preserved. The new cases require no functions
embedded in YAML, dependencies, environmental services, or host settings.

Validation evidence will be recorded after parsing the finished fixtures. No
implementation conformance has been tested. A downstream runner should prove
its comparator and assertion paths detect incorrect returns, in-place mutation,
aliased results, divergent replay, and unknown assertion fields using disposable
negative controls, without changing these authoritative fixtures.

## Remaining gaps and contract decisions

The contract does not specify uniformity, quality of randomness, seed diversity,
PRNG draw counts, or state advancement observable independently of replay. An
always-unchanged fresh copy is therefore not rejected. It also does not define
invalid-input errors, supported non-string element types, nested-element copy
depth, optional arguments, or explicit null handling; these are not invented as
fixture expectations. The finite cases do not exhaust sequence sizes or seeds,
and the boundary checks cannot detect temporary input mutation restored before
return. Tests for stronger guarantees require an explicit contract decision.

# Portable shuffle invariant fixtures

`SPEC.md` defines the behavior; `tests.yaml` contains data-driven checks of that
behavior. This document defines how a runner executes those checks. It adds no
distribution requirement or cross-language PRNG algorithm.

## Schema and comparison

`shuffle_invariants` is the case list. Each record has a unique, stable `name`,
an integer `seed`, and a `seq` list. The cases currently use only strings and
empty lists. Decode YAML strings exactly: compare Unicode code points without
normalization, case folding, locale collation, or trimming. In particular,
`"\u00e9"` and `"e\u0301"` are different element values.

Map the public `shuffle(seq, rng)` API to the implementation's idiomatic API.
Construct the implementation's RNG with `seed`; do not pass the integer as the
RNG argument unless the adapter constructs the RNG. All cases use seed 1. No
specific generator, seed-to-state mapping, or exact shuffled order is required.

The optional `draws` field is a positive integer, defaulting to 1. It counts
successive shuffle calls using one RNG instance; it is not a count of random
numbers consumed internally. Assertion fields, when present, must be boolean
`true`. An omitted assertion is not requested by that record. The original
`length` record remains a length-only check.

| Assertion | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| `preserves_length` | Every result has the length of the original input snapshot. |
| `preserves_multiset` | Every result has exactly the same element values and occurrence counts as the original snapshot. Set equality alone is insufficient. |
| `preserves_input` | After every call, the input still equals its original snapshot element by element, in the same order. Check it again after the final call. |
| `returns_new_sequence` | Every result is a fresh sequence container: it is distinct from the supplied input and from all retained earlier result containers in that stream, including for empty and singleton inputs. Equal contents are allowed. |
| `reproduces_stream` | Two fresh RNGs constructed with the same seed in the same implementation produce equal ordered result sequences for all `draws` calls. Compare each result element by element at the corresponding call index. |

These are observable checks, not instructions to evaluate fixture text as code.
No callable helpers are used. Fresh-container identity must be checked through
the runtime's object identity or an adapter that can establish fresh allocation;
value equality cannot establish it. A runner unable to observe that requirement
must report it as unsupported rather than omit it. Input non-mutation is checked
at call boundaries; these fixtures cannot detect a temporary mutation restored
before a call returns.

## Execution and replay protocol

1. Setup: decode the case, keep an independent value snapshot of `seq`, create
   a fresh input container, and create a fresh RNG seeded with `seed`.
2. Actions: call `shuffle` exactly `draws` times with that same input container
   and RNG. Do not reseed between calls, and do not feed a shuffled result into
   the next call. Retain every returned container so identity checks cannot be
   defeated by object-ID reuse. Capture an independent ordered value snapshot
   of each result immediately after the call.
3. Observations: run every requested per-call invariant against the original
   input snapshot and check final input non-mutation when requested. Check
   result identity before copying it; a runner must not hide aliasing by copying
   the implementation's result first.
4. Replay: when `reproduces_stream` is present, create a second fresh input
   container with the original values and a second fresh RNG with the same seed.
   Repeat steps 2 and 3 for that stream. Compare the two lists of result snapshots
   in call order, with exact element order inside each result. Keep the first
   stream's RNG alive during replay; the two RNGs must be separate instances.
5. Cleanup: release retained inputs, snapshots, results, and RNGs even on failure.
   Execute cases in isolation; do not share RNGs or change host process settings.

Reproducibility is local to a fixed implementation, runtime, and RNG
configuration. The runner records those details. There are two streams of 16
calls in each replay case; this is a finite replay check, not a statistical test.
There are no distribution thresholds or probabilistic acceptance criteria.
Never require two seeds to differ, a result to differ from its input, successive
calls to differ, or an exact cross-language stream. A fresh copy returned in
unchanged order can satisfy the current specification; uniformity and a
nontrivial permutation guarantee would require a separate contract decision.

## Required handling and accounting

Only `name`, `seed`, `seq`, `draws`, and the five assertion fields above are
recognized case fields. Unknown groups or fields must be reported as unsupported
requirements (or rejected as schema errors), never silently ignored. Malformed
known fields and duplicate names are schema errors. Normal calls are required
to succeed; an implementation error is a failed case, not a valid empty result.
No portable error category or error-message contract is defined here.

Count each case record once, regardless of its draws, streams, or assertions.
A case passes only if every requested assertion executes and passes. Report
setup, call, assertion, or cleanup failures with the case name and stage. An
unsupported assertion makes the case unsupported; retain any partial evidence.
Maintain `discovered = passed + failed + skipped + unsupported` and
`executed = passed + failed`. Full conformance requires all discovered cases to
pass; failures, skips, unsupported requirements, or zero discovered cases must
prevent a successful conformance exit.
